_comment: GROUND TRUTH. This file is USP-07 and it is the only thing that makes a
precision or recall number mean anything.
HOW THIS WAS AUTHORED, AND THE RULE FOR EDITING IT:
Every `expect` list below was derived by reading the scenario's CONFIGURATION
in testbed/synth.py - the cipher suite, the protocol version, the certificate,
the STARTTLS exchange - and reasoning about which rules SHOULD fire. None of it
was produced by running the analyser.
Never update this file by pasting in what the tool output. The moment the
expected results are generated by the thing under test, precision is 1.0 by
construction and the figure is worthless. If evaluate.py reports a
disagreement, decide which side is wrong on the merits: either the rule has a
`scope: fleet` marks a finding that cannot appear in a single-session capture
because it needs cross-session state - certificate substitution needs two
sessions to the same host. Those are scored against fleet.pcap only.
Capture names match testbed/synth.py SCENARIOS exactly. An earlier version of
this file listed 18 aspirational captures whose names matched nothing, which is
why evaluate.py could not be written against it.

certificates.valid: 2048-bit RSA, SHA-256, CN=mail-healthy.test, 90 days remaining, leaf + CA served
certificates.expiring: 1024-bit RSA, SHA-1 signature, CN=mail-degraded.test, 9 days remaining, leaf + CA served
certificates.expired_selfsigned: 2048-bit RSA, SHA-256, self-signed, CN=mail-compromised.test, expired 47 days ago, leaf only
certificates.missing_intermediate: 2048-bit RSA, SHA-256, CN=mail-partial.test, 90 days remaining, leaf served WITHOUT its CA

captures.name: smtp_starttls_healthy
captures.reasoning: TLS 1.3 with an AEAD suite and ephemeral key exchange, and a hybrid post-quantum group IS offered, so PQ-NOT-READY must not fire either. The certificate is encrypted at 1.3, so no CERT rule may fire - reporting one would mean inventing a finding from data we never saw. This capture is the false-positive guard: anything at all here is a false positive.

captures.name: smtp_starttls_stripped

configured.certificate: none - the session never reached TLS

captures.reasoning: The mangled capability is the stripping signature. ATTACK-AUTH-BEFORE-TLS must NOT also fire: it is written to cover the case where plaintext AUTH was offered but no credentials were actually seen, and here they were. STARTTLS-ADVERTISED-NOT-USED must not fire either, because the capability was removed rather than ignored.

captures.name: imaps_implicit_weak
captures.reasoning: Half of the USP-01 pair. The certificate is expired AND self-signed, so CERT-EXPIRED-SELF-SIGNED fires and the separate CERT-EXPIRED and CERT-SELF-SIGNED rules must not - three findings for one defect is noise. CERT-CHAIN-INCOMPLETE must not fire: a self-signed leaf is a complete chain of one. The key is 2048-bit and SHA-256, so no strength rule applies. Critical because this is a credential-bearing port (RFC 8314).

captures.name: smtp_relay_expired_cert

configured.certificate: expired_selfsigned - THE SAME BYTES as imaps_implicit_weak

captures.reasoning: The other half of the USP-01 pair, and the single most important row in this file. Identical certificate bytes to imaps_implicit_weak, but port 25 is opportunistic MTA-to-MTA relay (RFC 7435) where the sender has no trust anchor, so the same defect is informational. If these two ever report the same severity, the role-aware severity engine has regressed.

captures.name: imaps_downgrade
captures.reasoning: The server chose static RSA when the client offered ECDHE and TLS 1.3, losing forward secrecy - that is what the intersection anomaly exists to catch, and no rule looking only at the negotiated suite could see it. TLS-WEAK-DH-GROUP must NOT fire: ffdhe2048 is named in supported_groups but the key exchange is static RSA, so no DH group is actually in use. The certificate is sound, so no CERT rule applies.

captures.name: imap_advertised_not_used

configured.client_behaviour: ignored the upgrade and sent a plaintext LOGIN

captures.reasoning: A client-side policy failure, not an attack: the capability was intact and the client ignored it. ATTACK-AUTH-BEFORE-TLS must not fire - the server advertised LOGINDISABLED, which is the correct behaviour and cancels that finding.

captures.name: pop3_starttls_healthy
captures.reasoning: Cryptographically sound, but no hybrid post-quantum group is offered. Exercises the POP3 STLS keyword rather than SMTP/IMAP STARTTLS.

captures.name: smtp_relay_cleartext

configured.capability: STARTTLS advertised by the local server
configured.client_behaviour: remote peer MTA delivered without upgrading

captures.reasoning: The USP-01 negative control. STARTTLS-ADVERTISED-NOT-USED must NOT fire here even though the pattern matches, because on port 25 the client is a remote peer outside this organisation's control and SMTP-RELAY-NO-TLS already covers it. A tool that raises a HIGH here is the tool analysts mute.

captures.name: imaps_mid_session

configured.capture_starts: after the handshake completed - protected application data only

captures.reasoning: A normal forensic situation. The session is encrypted but uninspectable. Reporting it as cleartext would be a serious misread, and reporting nothing would let an uninspected host grade as clean (ADR-0014). No crypto rule may fire: we saw no handshake.

captures.name: imaps_tls12_valid_chain
captures.reasoning: The S5 happy path: unlike TLS 1.3 the chain is observable, complete, in date, correctly named and RSA-verifiable against the test root. Any CERT finding here is a false positive.

captures.name: imaps_expiring_cert
captures.reasoning: Three independent certificate defects that must be reported separately because they have different fixes. CERT-WEAK-KEY and CERT-WEAK-SIGNATURE are CERTIFICATE_STRENGTH and must NOT be role-adjusted (ADR-0010) - a 1024-bit key is weak everywhere. Forward secrecy is present via ECDHE, so TLS-NO-FORWARD-SECRECY must not fire despite the CBC suite.

captures.name: imaps_cert_substitution_a
captures.reasoning: Sound on its own. It only becomes evidence when paired with session b.

captures.name: imaps_cert_substitution_b

configured.sni: mail-healthy.test but the certificate is CN=mail-partial.test
configured.host: the SAME host and port as imaps_cert_substitution_a

captures.reasoning: The leaf is served without its CA, so some clients build a path and others do not - the intermittent delivery failure administrators chase for weeks. The name also does not match the SNI. ATTACK-CERT-SUBSTITUTION is scope=fleet: it needs both sessions in one capture and cannot appear when this scenario is analysed alone.
